title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf: Adversarial Misclassification of Safe Inputs as Unsafe in Multimodal Guardrails

problem.claim: Adversaries may induce multimodal guard models to reject legitimate requests containing benign inputs, degrading service availability and eroding trust.

gap.claim: Existing adversarial research has focused extensively on jailbreaking attacks that produce false negatives, while inducing false positives on benign inputs remains unexplored.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Unsafe Induction Attacks, which use imperceptibly perturbed safe images to trigger guard-model rejection of legitimate user requests.
The paper proposes Unsafe Semantic Distillation, which aligns adversarial perturbations with distributional representations of unsafe content rather than prompt-specific instances.
The work identifies an availability failure mode in deployed safety filters and vulnerabilities in current multimodal safety architectures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four state-of-the-art guard models and realistic user simulation scenarios, USD achieved an 84% attack success rate.
USD outperformed existing methods in the reported evaluations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal guard models are used as safety components for screening content in vision-language systems.
False-negative jailbreaking attacks have been extensively studied, but adversarial false positives on benign inputs remain unexplored.
Unsafe Induction Attacks use imperceptibly perturbed safe images to cause guard models to reject legitimate requests.
Unsafe Semantic Distillation aligns adversarial perturbations with distributional representations of unsafe content across diverse prompts.
The authors report an 84% attack success rate across four guard models and realistic user simulations, outperforming existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Adversarial perturbations aligned with distributional representations of unsafe content can induce false-positive rejections across diverse user prompts.

interpretation.claim: Prompt-agnostic semantic alignment may generalize attacks beyond prompt-specific instances.

application.claim: Evaluate multimodal guardrails for false-positive availability failures using diverse prompts and semantically aligned perturbations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves outside the reported models, scenarios, or perturbation conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the attack algorithm, perturbation constraints, or threat-model assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the four guard models or existing comparison methods.
The abstract does not provide evaluation datasets, statistical variation, or per-model results.
The abstract does not report defenses or mitigation strategies.
